subject.title: [BUG]: Browser tool: `snapshot` returns page content before scroll, ignoring viewport position

question: Should the browser tool default snapshot remain a whole-page structural read with added scroll metadata, or should OpenClaw add/make default a visible-viewport-scoped snapshot after scroll?
rationale: The source-level behavior is clear, but the expected contract is not documented and changing it affects model-facing browser semantics, compatibility with full-page workflows, and multiple browser backends.

options.title: Add explicit viewport-aware snapshot mode
options.body: Introduce viewport-scoped output or scroll/viewport metadata behind a clear mode first, keep the current full-tree path available, and choose the default after live proof.

options.title: Change the default to visible viewport
options.body: Make snapshot output match the current viewport after scroll, with an explicit full/raw escape hatch for existing workflows.

options.title: Document full-tree behavior only
options.body: Keep current snapshot semantics and document that agents should use labels/screenshots or selector-scoped snapshots when viewport evidence matters.

recommendation.title: Add explicit viewport-aware snapshot mode
recommendation.body: Introduce viewport-scoped output or scroll/viewport metadata behind a clear mode first, keep the current full-tree path available, and choose the default after live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current snapshot route and helper history in this checkout point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for the browser snapshot contract decision.
